The maximum is 2^999 − 2^499, which none of the three solutions gives.

**Upper bound.** Let σ be the reflection A ↦ A′. A set A and its complement Aᶜ are disjoint, so P contains at most one set from each complementary pair {A, Aᶜ}. That gives |P| ≤ 2^999.

σ commutes with complementation. Suppose A′ = Aᶜ. Then condition 3 forces A′ = Aᶜ into P whenever A is in P, and A ∩ Aᶜ = ∅ violates condition 2. So no such A can be in P.

These sets are exactly those that contain one element from each of the 500 pairs {i, 1001−i}. There are 2^500 of them, forming 2^499 complementary pairs. Excluding them gives |P| ≤ 2^999 − 2^499.

**Construction.** Consider the remaining complementary pairs {A, Aᶜ}. σ sends each such pair to a pair {A′, A′ᶜ}.
- If σ fixes the pair with A′ = A, choose A.
- If σ maps it to a different pair, choose A from one and A′ from the other.
- A′ = Aᶜ has been excluded, so no other case occurs.

This choice is closed under σ and takes exactly one set from each allowed complementary pair. Any two chosen sets then intersect. Two sets with B ≠ Aᶜ can be disjoint only if one is contained in the complement of the other, and the choice rules out this case. The family has size 2^999 − 2^499.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives 2^999, which exceeds the upper bound.
- Solution 2 gives 3·2^997, which is smaller than the maximum.
- Solution 3 gives 2^999 − C(1000,500)/2 + C(998,498). C(1000,500)/2 is about 10^297, far larger than 2^499 (about 10^150), so this is also smaller than the maximum.

CHOICE: NONE
